subject: Life Skills
title: Why We Procrastinate
description: A short lesson to help you apply Why We Procrastinate.

hook.text: He had two weeks to finish the project. He started the night before. This was not laziness — it was fear.

buildup.text: Procrastination is not a time problem. Psychologist Timothy Pychyl calls it an emotion regulation problem.

discovery.text: You avoid the task because it triggers negative emotions — boredom, anxiety, self-doubt, or helplessness.

twist.text: Your brain picks short-term relief over long-term gain. Scrolling your phone feels better right now than writing.

climax.text: The fix is not discipline. It is lowering the emotional barrier. Start with the tiniest possible first step.

punchline.text: You are not lazy. The task just scares you. Start small.

quiz.question: What is procrastination really about?
options: An emotion regulation problem tied to negative feelings about the task
